A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Associative Transformer study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification and Sort-of-CLEVR experiments, component ablations, and attention and memory analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original classification, relational-reasoning and diagnostic results, and adds AiT-Base reasoning results and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The squash layer, low-rank memory, bottleneck attention, balance loss and Hopfield retrieval match. However, v2 Equation 4 weights old memory by alpha, whereas v3 Equation 3 weights new memory by alpha. V3 mentions alpha = 0.1 in Section 3.3 but retains 0.9 in the experimental settings. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is reparameterization, an error or an actual update change.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Triangle, Oxford-IIIT Pet and Sort-of-CLEVR, including its relational and non-relational tasks. Additional model results and computational measurements do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds BRIMs and Luna to the reported Triangle comparison; previously their Triangle entries were missing. The relational-reasoning comparison removes CNN+RN. CNN+MLP becomes CNN+LSTM with the same citation and 60.08/99.47 scores, so this relabeling does not establish a newly evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: V3 introduces FLOP-based evaluation with Hopfield deletion and replacement controls, and evaluates AiT-Base on Sort-of-CLEVR alongside AiT-Small. It also changes the stated W/O Hopfield reference architecture from Figure 1b's self-attention to Figure 1a's cross-attention, without establishing that the experiment was rerun. Dataset preprocessing and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds Hopfield computational-cost ablations and a qualitative report of test-batch-size insensitivity. It removes v2 Appendix A.5's memory-forward ablation, the dense-only classification ablation, and positional-embedding memory initialization. The attention-head, temperature, energy and patch-diversity analyses remain, although several move between the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report means of three individual experiments and retain the same uncertainty bands in the Pet learning curves. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance testing is introduced.

E6.justification: V3 adds Triangle scores for BRIMs (58.34%) and Luna (57.26%), with recomputed averages; AiT-Base reasoning scores of 80.03% relational and 99.98% non-relational; and FLOP measurements. CNN+RN and the removed ablation results disappear. Matched AiT classification and AiT-Small reasoning scores are unchanged. V3 also calls 71.49% the best single-block performance, although the retained plot includes C+LM+SA at 71.62%, identified as best in v2.

T1.justification: V3 omits v2 Section 4.1's explicit complexity-reduction argument from O((BN)^2) to O(BNk). The Hopfield energy formulation, convergence rationale and balance-loss mathematics are retained. The added supervised-classification notation mainly documents the existing training setup; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contribution of specialized priors combined with Hopfield retrieval remains. V3 adds an explicit dataset-wide state-of-the-art claim for Sort-of-CLEVR and drops the abstract's assertion of complexity invariance to input quantities and dimensions. Parameter and layer efficiency receive greater emphasis.

C2.justification: V3 extends the existing temperature-tuning caveat to difficulties scaling to larger datasets without tuning temperature and bottleneck size. Appendix D adds an image-versus-text dependency explanation for ViT/BERT sparsity differences. Section 3.3 newly attributes reported batch-size insensitivity to the memory-update decay.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies PyTorch, four A100 GPUs, test batch size one, and the classification loss combined with the balance loss. These are disclosures rather than established changes to existing experiments. Conversely, it removes v2's detailed explanation of temporary test-time memory computation without persistent updates. Both versions only promise future public code availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds mixture-of-experts positioning with Allingham et al. and Zuo et al., and removes Minsky's citation. The GWT comparison table revises architectural classifications, including marking AiT as using self-attention. Most cited works and the central distinction from existing sparse Transformers remain; consolidated duplicate references and publication updates do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition and experimental narrative, and shortens the title. The standalone attention-head inspection moves into Appendix D, temperature analysis moves into Appendix F, and prior specialization becomes a dedicated experimental subsection. Contributions and ablations are reorganized into lists.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation of displays. Figure 1 is redrawn with an explicit six-layer versus twelve-layer comparison. V3 adds a FLOP table, removes the test-time schematic and associated tables, drops the reasoning table's average column, and revises figure labels and captions.

improvement.justification: The FLOP evidence, additional results and clearer organization are useful. However, v3 claims dataset-wide Sort-of-CLEVR state of the art while omitting CNN+RN, reported at 81.07% relational accuracy in v2, without reconciling it with the new AiT-Base result of 80.03%. Removing the test-time explanation and ablation, together with the inconsistent EWMA coefficients and settings, also reduces transparency and reproducibility. These reliability losses outweigh the limited gains.
